input: Send thank-you cards after the holiday dinner

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether cards go to all guests, hosts, gift-givers only, or a mix determines how many cards are needed and what the messages should cover.
Understanding who the recipients are (family, colleagues, close friends, acquaintances) shapes the tone and level of personalization required for each card.
The specific holiday and how recently the dinner occurred determines urgency — thank-you cards sent two weeks late feel very different from those sent within a few days.
A budget limit affects whether cards are handwritten on premium stationery, store-bought, or designed and sent digitally.
The desired tone (warm and personal vs. brief and polished) and whether messages should be unique per recipient or use a shared template will shape the writing effort.
Whether cards are physical (requiring addresses, stamps, and mailing) or digital (email, e-card service) completely changes the steps and timeline involved.
Knowing what the user considers a job well done — all cards sent by a certain date, every recipient acknowledged individually, a particular sentimental quality — sets the bar for the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Send thank-you cards after holiday dinner
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to send thank-you cards to people following a holiday dinner, covering everything from who receives them to how and when they get sent.

questions.title: Who exactly are you sending cards to?
questions.description: Clarify whether cards go to every guest, only the host(s), gift-givers, or some other subset of attendees.

questions.title: What is your relationship to the recipients?
questions.description: Determine whether recipients are close family, friends, colleagues, or a mix, which affects the appropriate tone and level of personalization.

questions.title: How soon after the dinner do you want these sent?
questions.description: Establish the target send date or deadline to set the urgency and pacing of the task.

questions.title: Are you sending physical cards or digital ones?
questions.description: Decide between handwritten/mailed cards and digital options like email or an e-card service, as this changes every downstream step.

questions.title: What is your budget for cards and postage?
questions.description: Understand spending limits to recommend appropriate card options, from premium stationery to free digital alternatives.

questions.title: Should each message be personal or use a shared template?
questions.description: Find out if the user wants a unique, tailored note for every recipient or a single warm message adapted slightly for each card.

questions.title: What does a successfully completed round of cards look like?
questions.description: Identify the user's definition of done — all cards sent by a date, every guest individually acknowledged, a certain sentimental quality achieved, etc.
